answer.summary: Stein said Instagram prioritized serving its own users, not copying for its own sake: Stories addressed Instagram users’ need for an easy, lower-pressure way to share ephemeral photos, while adapting the format to Instagram’s purpose and audience.

sections.heading: User need and product fit
sections.content: Stein said the team focused on Instagram users and wanted to give them an easy way to share a photo that would disappear. They saw this as fitting Instagram’s purpose—sharing life and connecting with people—while an ephemeral, like-free format could lower the pressure to post and work well on mobile. He credited Snapchat with inventing the format, but argued that teams should learn from ideas elsewhere and make them serve their own product’s users. Instagram Stories complemented rather than replaced the feed.

sections.heading: Making the format Instagram’s own
sections.content: Rather than contorting the established Instagram feed into an ephemeral product, the team built a distinct experience and added Instagram-specific choices. Stein cited creative tools such as neon drawing and sophisticated filters, allowing people to upload high-quality photos from their camera roll (which Snapchat then did not allow), and adding a press-and-hold pause because Stories could move too quickly. These changes helped Stories feel native to Instagram rather than simply being “some other thing.”
